jobs.description: Employer: Packaging Corporation of America Expires: 11/09/2026 As a Fortune 500 company, Packaging Corporation of America (PCA) is an ideas and solutions company. Our corrugated packaging business seeks to be the leader in helping our customers — large and small — package, transport and display products of all kinds. Our white paper business delivers Paper With Purpose by providing the highest level of customer service and operational excellence. We have approximately 15,000 team members in more than 100 locations in the United States that strive to meet the local needs of our customers. Our mission is to serve the needs of our customers, today and tomorrow, with products and services that exceed expectations for performance and environmental responsibility. People • Customers • Trust Program Overview: PCA’s 13-week (May – August) Sales Summer Internship offers hands-on experience across key departments of Design, Production, Customer Service, and Sales while building foundational sales knowledge. Interns will also participate in a corporate office visit in Lake Forest, IL to engage with marketing, meet with PCA leadership, and network with fellow summer interns. Upon successful completion of the program, interns may be offered a full-time position to begin after graduation into PCA’s GIFT Program (rotational sales development program). jobs.title: Marketing Project Management Intern at The Henry Ford
jobs.description: Employer: The Henry Ford Expires: 11/09/2026 The Henry Ford is a nonprofit organization, an internationally recognized cultural destination, and a one-of-a-kind workplace. Our team is inspired daily by one another as well as the authentic stories of innovation that we share across our four venues. The Ford Foundation Equity Initiative (FFEI) Internship Program is a cohort program that offers professional development, mentorship, and networking opportunities. We invite candidates from diverse backgrounds who are curious about careers in the museum field to become part of our legacy and carry it forward. Interested candidates will submit a brief statement of purpose (250-500 words) outlining:Why they are interested in this internshipHow this opportunity aligns with their academic, personal, or career goalsThe skills, experiences, or perspectives they would bring to the teamWhat they hope to learn and accomplish during the internship The Ford Foundation Equity Initiative Internship Program Overview and Time Commitment The FFEI Internship Program’s mission is to offer opportunities in museum work to emerging professionals who identify with historically marginalized groups and to invite our interns to think outside the box and explore their careers in new ways.Participants will engage in the program through various bi-weekly professional development workshops hosted on our Dearborn campus. Bi-weekly workshop attendance and participation are mandatory. Applicants should work with their leadership to ensure proper attendance. Workshops typically occur on Wednesdays during the work week. As part of your employment, we also have our interns participate in an end of cohort survey. Note: All candidates interested in FFEI Internship roles must have full Wednesday (9am-5pm) availability due to bi-weekly workshop programmatic requirements of the internship. The 15-week Winter 2027 internship runs January 25–May 7, 2027. Attendance at orientation on January 25 is mandatory. The Marketing Project Management Intern will help the Creative Services and Marketing teams keep projects organized and moving forward. Working under the guidance of a project lead, the intern will track timelines, gather updates, coordinate meetings, and communicate with teams across the institution. The internship offers practical experience with the people, tools, and processes involved in delivering marketing and design projects.This is a hybrid position, with most work performed remotely. Based on project needs, the intern may be required to work onsite at The Henry Ford's campus in Dearborn, MI. Essential ResponsibilitiesHelp coordinate multiple marketing and design projects, tracking tasks, deadlines, and next steps in WorkfrontGather weekly status updates from team members and keep project information currentHelp document project scope, timelines, and potential risks, bringing changes or concerns to the project lead’s attentionOrganize and schedule team meetings, prepare materials, and document decisions and follow-up itemsCommunicate project updates to internal partners with guidance from the project leadContact external vendors, request quotes, and organize information needed for project decisionsReview project progress and suggest ways to improve workflows and communicationLearn and follow Creative Services project management processes and assist with updates to those processesAttend scheduled virtual meetings during Eastern Time business hours and respond to project communications in a timely mannerParticipate in required internship orientation and professional development activities QualificationsCurrently enrolled in or recently graduated from a college or university program in marketing, business, communications, project management, or a related fieldWorking knowledge of Microsoft OfficeAbility to learn Workfront and other tools used to organize projects and filesAvailability on Wednesdays for required internship programmingAbility to attend scheduled meetings during Eastern Time business hours and work onsite in Dearborn when required Special SkillsStrong organizational skills and attention to detail when tracking multiple assignments and deadlinesClear written and verbal communication with team members and internal partnersAbility to follow up on tasks, ask questions, and bring potential delays to the project lead’s attentionAbility to work independently while staying connected with a collaborative virtual teamInterest in how marketing and design projects move from request to completionFamiliarity with cloud-based file storage, digital asset management systems, or project management tools is helpful but not required PHYSICAL/MENTAL/ENVIRONMENTALPhysical: Work is primarily performed at a computer. Other physical requirements are minimal or not applicableMental: Requires organization, attention to detail, problem solving, and the ability to track several projects with different deadlinesEnvironment: Work is primarily remote, with onsite work at The Henry Ford’s Dearborn campus based on project and internship program needs Internship Program CompensationInterns are paid under the following paygrades:First year intern in school (undergraduate or trade): $17.00 First year intern with completed degree (undergraduate or trade): $18.00Graduate school and postgraduates: $20.00

jobs.title: Internal Audit & Accounting Intern-Raleigh, NC at Gilbarco Veeder-Root
jobs.description: Employer: Gilbarco Veeder-Root Expires: 11/09/2026 Are you energized by being a key contributor on a highly talented team? Intellectually curious? Do you want to apply what have you learned in school, while doing so at a global, public company? Would you like to gain real world experience to begin the foundation of your career? If this sounds like you, then join us as an Internal Audit Intern at Vontier.This position reports to the Internal Audit Manager and will be hybrid (1-2 days onsite) based in our Raleigh, NC headquarters. Start date intended as soon as possible following an offer acceptance.The rate for this position is $24/hr.Working with the Internal Audit team, you will be involved in a broad theme of topics and responsibilities including (but not limited to):Assist the company in achieving continued compliance with the Sarbanes-Oxley Act ("SOX") including participating in scoping, planning, walkthroughs, testing, status reporting, and communicating with external auditors.Participating in a wide variety of financial, operational, and information technology (IT) internal audits.Participates in gathering and analyzing data through a variety of methods including interviews, financial research, etc.Assist in developing and presenting findings and recommendations based on audit work performed to improve internal controls.Prepare detailed work papers for each project assigned.Assist in drafting Internal Audit reports identifying the scope, issues identified, recommendations and management action plans.Interacts and communicates with business process owners and upper-level management as needed during internal audit activities.Participate in other internal audit projects as assigned. WHO YOU ARE (Qualifications)Must be currently pursuing a Master’s degree in Accounting.Strong listening and communication skills.Intellectual curiosity.Humility and teamwork; ability to take feedback and coaching and adapt to new challenges.Strong personal organization and prioritization skills.Uncompromising ethics and integrity.Strong quantitative, financial and analytical skills.The internship period may last up to 12 months for 20-30 hours per week (you will have control of the hours / days you work based on your academic commitments).The base compensation for this position is $24 per hour. Your actual base salary will be determined based upon numerous factors which may include relevant experience, skills, location (labor market data), credentials (education, certifications), and internal equity. This opportunity does not offer relocation support.

jobs.title: 2027 Summer Intern, Program Delivery (California) at ICF
jobs.description: Employer: ICF Expires: 11/09/2026 We are hiring Program Operations, Program Delivery and Program Outreach Interns who support the planning, execution, and monitoring of energy efficiency programs within ICF's Utility, Programs and Services division. These roles provide hands-on experience in program operations and offers a valuable opportunity to apply academic knowledge in a professional setting.As an intern, you will collaborate with cross-functional teams, contribute to the development of high-quality products and services, and gain exposure to major projects and client interactions. This experience is designed to help build foundational skills in project management, communication, and teamwork, while deepening your understanding of energy-efficient technologies and utility-sponsored programs.This is an entry-level, 10-week, full time internship that begins in early June 2027. Pay is expected to be $23 per hour for undergraduate students and $28 per hour for graduate students. These roles will be hybrid from Los Angeles, CA, San Francisco, CA, Irvine, CA, or San Diego, CA. At this time, we are unable to provide relocation nor housing assistance.As a Program Operations Intern, you will:Coordinate and support the execution of program activities, events, tasks, and deliverables.Conduct research and analyze data on market trends, customer segments, competitive landscapes, and energy efficiency equipment to support program planning and decision-making.Evaluate market potential, program growth opportunities, and distributor, contractor, and trade ally networks.Collaborate with Sales, Account Management, Engineering, and other team members to develop aligned outreach, sales, customer targeting, decarbonization, equity and affordability, lead generation, and value proposition strategies.Prepare and maintain reports, schedules, meeting minutes, and other program documentation.Summarize findings and present actionable recommendations that support data-driven decisions and the development of accurate, timely, high-quality products and services.Provide administrative and communications support, including coordinating meetings and helping teams complete priorities on time.As a Program Delivery Intern, you will:Support the Program Delivery team by developing client presentations and communicating key program results to internal and external stakeholders.Identify and develop program opportunities that advance clients' clean energy goals.Review program processes and recommend opportunities to improve efficiency and delivery.Coordinate with program implementation teams and cross-functional partners, including Marketing, IT, and Customer Care.Engage participating service providers to gather information and identify opportunities for program improvement, depending on the role.Prepare and review technical specifications and calculations for energy efficiency measures and projects, depending on the required skill set.As a Program Outreach Intern, you will:Provide support for field-based staff and the network of participating Trade AlliesSupport communications with participating contractors, customers, and consultants.Clarify and resolve/escalate customer/contractor concerns related to program participation as necessary.Collaborate with regional and national teams to provide national cohesiveness and bring efficiency & best practices to your client's programs.Support and track contractor enrollment in programs.Assist technical teams to ensure QA/QC standards for the program are met.Individuals with a focus-area preference (Operations, Delivery or Outreach) should note such on their cover letter or resume, otherwise, applicants may be considered for any of the above teams. Basic QualificationsBy start date, a minimum of 30 completed college-level credit hours is required preferably in Business Administration, Economics, Project Management, Energy Management, or a related field.Must be able to pass any required background check(s), which may include drug screening.Due to contract requirements, U.S. Citizenship or Permanent Work Authorization is requiredPreferred QualificationsA completed bachelor's degree and enrollment verification or 9 credits completed in a graduate program in Business Administration, Economics, Project Management, Energy Management, or a related field.Strong organizational, time management, task prioritization, and attention-to-detail skills.Excellent written, verbal, analytical, and collaborative communication skills.Ability to work independently and effectively as part of a team.Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite, particularly Excel, PowerPoint, and Word.Experience with program coordination, documentation, research, data collection, market analysis, or sales planning projects.Familiarity with data analytics and visualization tools such as Power BI, Power Query, or VBA.Interest in energy efficiency, market research, and sales strategy; familiarity with HVAC, water heating, space heating, kitchen equipment, or lighting technologies is a plus.

jobs.title: Technical Project Analyst at MACOM
jobs.description: Employer: MACOM Expires: 11/09/2026 MACOM (NASDAQ: MTSI) is a global leader in the design and manufacture of advanced semiconductor products across a diverse range of end markets, including Data Centers, Telecommunications, Industrial and Aerospace and Defense. We develop innovative, cutting-edge technologies and products across the spectrum of radio frequency (RF), microwave, millimeter wave, photonics and high-speed analog technologies. Our solutions support critical network infrastructure applications like artificial intelligence, high performance computing, satellite communications, radar, unmanned aerial vehicles, medical equipment, test and measurement and advanced wireless networks. MACOM has more than 75 years of expertise in semiconductor process development, wafer fabrication, circuit design, advanced packaging, systems architecture and applications engineering. We are committed to our customers’ success. We partner with customers to help solve their most challenging problems by providing semiconductor solutions that are at the forefront of the highest power, highest frequency and/or highest data rates. Leading technologies, innovative products and driven employees. Come be a part of MACOM and help advance the next generation of connectivity infrastructure! Technical Project Analyst: PMO & Security OperationsThe Team & Your RoleThis role sits at the intersection of project execution and information security operations. You will support MACOM's Information Security team by helping build out a PMO function, covering the dashboards that track security initiatives, the processes that keep projects on schedule, and the standards that scale the program over time. This position is designed to develop well-rounded project management skills, with the expectation that you will grow into independently managing projects as you gain experience. Core Responsibilities• Develop and apply core project management skills including scope definition, scheduling, risk tracking, and stakeholder communication across active security initiatives.• Support project managers in planning and executing projects, with increasing ownership over time as skills and familiarity with the team's portfolio grow.• Build and maintain PMO dashboards and reporting tools in Power BI, Airtable, ServiceNow, or similar platforms to provide real-time visibility into project status, milestones, resource utilization, and risk across the security portfolio.• Support the Information Security team in tracking deliverables, deadlines, dependencies, and action items across concurrent initiatives.• Collect, clean, and synthesize project data from multiple sources to produce accurate and actionable status reports for stakeholders.• Assist in coordinating cross-functional meetings, capturing meeting minutes, and following up on open items to maintain project momentum.• Contribute to the design and documentation of PMO processes, templates, and governance standards that will serve as the foundation of the program.• Identify gaps in current project tracking workflows and recommend tooling or process improvements to increase team efficiency.• Support the evaluation and potential implementation of PPM (Project Portfolio Management) tooling to centralize and scale program visibility across the security organization. Qualifications• Pursuing a Bachelor's degree in Business, Information Systems, Engineering Management, Cybersecurity, or a related field.• Familiarity with project management concepts (e.g., Agile, Waterfall, or hybrid methodologies).• Experience building dashboards or reports using tools such as Power BI, Airtable, Excel, or similar platforms.• Strong organizational skills and attention to detail, with the ability to manage multiple tasks simultaneously.• Nice to Have: Exposure to PPM or work management tools (e.g., ServiceNow, Smartsheet, Jira, Monday.com, MS Project), basic familiarity with information security concepts, and knowledge of data visualization best practices. During the 12 weeks each Intern will:• Be given an individual and well-defined project with set outcome goals• Gain hands on experience• Receive excellent training and ongoing supervision• Be invited to attend an intern webinar series• Attend networking/social events• Attend and present at Poster Session about each Interns project successes and pitfalls• Receive formal, written feedback The Hourly Range for this position is $20 – $47 per hour. Actual salary offered to candidate will depend on several factors, including but not limited to, work location, relevant candidates’ experience, education, and specific knowledge, skills, and abilities. ITAR Due to ITAR regulations, only candidates who are U.S. Persons (U.S. citizens, U.S. nationals, lawful permanent residents, or individuals granted asylum or refugee status) will be considered for this position. EEO:MACOM is an Equal Opportunity Employer committed to a diverse workforce. MACOM will not discriminate against any worker or job applicant on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, national origin, age, disability, genetic information, veteran status, military service, marital status, or any other category protected under applicable law. jobs.description: Employer: The Autoimmune Fund Expires: 11/09/2026 About The Autoimmune FundAutoimmune and immune-mediated diseases affect millions of people, most of them women. About Us:The Indiana Biosciences Research Institute (IBRI) is a first-in-class translational medicine institute dedicated to advancing life sciences in the race to eliminate disease and improve human health and life.By connecting early-stage biotech companies with cutting-edge life science discoveries —and backed by the mission and resources of industry leaders, investors, and philanthropic partners—IBRI is successfully evolving a new, independent model to conquer disease, uniting previously fragmented forces in the quest for cures.Carefully curating and supporting early-stage companies with investment, talent, and space, IBRI strategically accelerates drug discovery. Our work benefits from the relatively low cost of living and doing business here, allowing more resources to be directed toward science.Fueled by the same entrepreneurial creativity as the groundbreaking scientific work we support, IBRI’s labs advance research across the frontiers of diabetes, metabolic disease, Alzheimer’s disease, and rare pediatric diseases. Our ambitious public–private vision cultivates talent while efficiently bridging the gap between research-driven inquiry and profit-driven drug development.At IBRI, cures are launched on a clear pathway to clinical trials, enabled by the combined resources and experience of our academic and industry partners, without the typical pressure to deliver rapid results for commercialization. IBRI labs pursue breakthroughs that might never happen elsewhere. Breakthroughs are happening here. Our novel financing model ensures that when discoveries are ready for clinical trials, the intellectual property is sold back to industry or spun off, creating a direct stream of revenue.By every measure, the IBRI model demonstrates a novel approach that delivers rewards. Scientific bench work is nurtured, drug discovery is advanced, workforce development is continuous, investors see returns, and donors see impact. Most importantly, IBRI’s structure and portfolio of accomplishments matter to the patients whose lives are improved—or even saved—by this forward-looking approach to life sciences.IBRI is driven to bring next-generation therapies to market with an understanding of the complex pressures that often bind innovation to economics. After more than a decade, the evidence is clear: IBRI is poised to transform life sciences—and for millions of people, even life itself.Equal Employment Opportunity:The IBRI provides equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants and does not discriminate based on age, race, color, religion, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, national origin, protected veteran status, disability, or any other legally protected status.

jobs.title: Engineering Co-Op: Spring 2027 at Safran Electrical & Power
jobs.description: Employer: Safran Electrical & Power - Safran Electrical & Power Expires: 11/11/2026 We're looking for students interested in working hands-on on real engineering projects. We offer Spring, Summer, and Fall rotations in a handful of areas (see below for more info). Our goal is to bridge the gap between classroom and real experience. Our hope is for students to feel like the work they're doing is valuable whilst challenging. Depending on a candidate's specialties and assigned area, roles require the following: Passion for mechanical, electrical, computer, or aerospace engineering, manufacturing, and technology. Strong analytical ability to solve problems and ability to learn quickly. Strong written & verbal communication skills to generate process instructions and reports. Ability to follow a structured project management process including document meeting minutes, action items, and monitor progress. Capability and tenacity for solving unique engineering problems. Ability to learn quickly and a desire to keep improving skills and to teach others when possible. Team player with a highly proactive and positive attitude with ability to work on own or in a team as needed. Hands-on skills. Demonstrated interest in building and testing. Regular, predictable attendance is required. Please note that estimated time for start/end dates are based on Spring 2027. Other semesters will have different dates. Want to know more about each of our Area Assignments? Let our managers tell you! Conversion Engineering: The Conversion Engineering Team is responsible for controller-generators and starter-generators (as well as converting the power they produce). We design and support multiple products with our current new product introduction (NPI) programs. The Mechanical Engineering Team designs the housings and assembly methods for our systems, ensuring they meet strict environmental and operational requirements. Their work is essential to delivering robust and reliable solutions for our aerospace applications. Embedded Systems Engineering: If you're curious about how hardware and software come together to power real-world systems and are eager to make an impact while learning from experienced engineers - join our Embedded Systems Engineering team. Industrialization Engineering: Industrialization is the perfect blend of design and manufacturing work. We have a mix of both in reviewing engineering drawings, discussing design features, developing solutions, mitigating design risks, managing prototype builds, building tooling, and implementing new products into production. We get the benefit of working with every department in the business and every day is different. If you want to have a mix of design work behind a desk and time on the production floor seeing designs you helped create come to life - then Industrialization is right for you! Manufacturing Engineering: As a Co-Op, you will work directly with our production team and design engineers to support the assembly and troubleshooting of aircrafts power-conversion units. We perform root-cause analysis on units that fail functional testing, remove roadblocks for our production team, diagnose defective parts, improve assembly processes, update work instructions, and initiate corrective actions. If you want hands-on experience on the shop floor and to improve efficiency while reducing waste - apply for Manufacturing Engineering. Production Support Engineering: Working in Production Support Engineering you will have the opportunity to work on real products and support day-to-day engineering activities that directly impact production, product reliability, and customer satisfaction. Responsibilities may include assisting with failure investigations, supporting resolution of production and supplier-related issues, evaluating nonconforming hardware, participating in repair and overhaul activities, reviewing engineering documentation, and contributing to engineering changes that improve product performance, manufacturability, and long-term supportability. Project Management: Everything starts with an idea, and project managers bring ideas into reality. From managing and executing plans, creative problem solving, and balancing the needs and expectations of a cross-functional team; project managers touch every aspect of the business and the world around us. With Project Management at Safran you will get real world understanding of how products and projects come to life, leveraging the strength of the team and how to manage risks and budget along the way. Quality Engineering: If you're looking to help ensure customer satisfaction and promote continual improvement of our products and processes, then the Quality Team may be for you. Our team is responsible for maintaining our Quality Management System (QMS), facilitating Advanced Product Quality Planning (APQP), and conducting internal quality audits. We promote continual improvement in the form of corrective actions and improvement projects. Rotating Machines Engineering: The mechanical design team within the Rotating Machines Department excels in engineering robust and high-performance aircraft rotating machinery. This includes generators and starter-generator systems. This group specializes in designing critical mechanical components such as rotors, stators, shafts, bearings, splines, and housings to ensure reliability and efficiency under demanding aerospace conditions. Supply Chain Engineering: Supply Chain is where ideas are transformed into finished products. We partner closely with suppliers to secure everything the business requires—from engineering components to the materials, equipment, and services that support daily operations. You'll gain firsthand experience in turning plans into reality by collaborating with suppliers, resolving challenges, and ensuring materials flow efficiently throughout the process. Systems/ Analysis Engineering: The System Integration & Performance Team develops, integrates, and validates aerospace electrical power systems by bringing together hardware, software, and control systems into a complete solution. Team members support system testing, performance analysis, troubleshooting, and certification activities to ensure products meet customer and regulatory requirements. Test Engineering: The Test Engineering Team specializes in test design, execution, and reporting for all power units. The team is composed of both test engineers and test equipment engineers. The test engineers handle the design, setup, execution, reporting of research and development testing, and qualification testing of new products and/or systems. Meanwhile, the test equipment engineering team design mechanical, electrical, and control equipment for the test lab to enable both production and new product testing to take place. Through Life Support Engineering: The Through Life Support Engineering team works on the problems that happen after designs enter production. The team investigates failures (both in the field and on the production line), solves production and supplier issues, supports repair and overhaul activity, evaluates nonconforming hardware, manages obsolescence, and develops design and drawing changes that keep products operating safely and reliably throughout their service life. For Co-Ops, it is a great opportunity to work on real hardware, see how engineering decisions affect the entire product lifecycle, and gain hands-on experience through a wide variety of technical challenges compared to working on a piece of a long-term development program.

jobs.feedName: David Nazarian College of Business & Economics
jobs.title: Financial Services Sales Program, Internship at Northwestern Mutual - Orange County
jobs.description: Employer: Northwestern Mutual - Orange County Expires: 11/11/2026 OverviewThe Financial Services Sales Program is a paid, 12-week early-career experience where students have an opportunity to explore the path to becoming a Northwestern Mutual Financial Representative. Through comprehensive training, personalized coaching, mentorship, and real client-facing experience, you'll develop foundational sales, relationship-building, and communication skills while exploring whether an entrepreneurial advisor career is right for you. In this hands-on program, you'll operate as an independent contractor, learning how financial advisors help clients navigate important financial decisions by understanding their goals, identifying their needs, and creating personalized financial plans. You can build a go-to-market strategy and business plan, learn how advisors conduct client conversations about financial goals and needs, and understand how they help guide individuals toward solutions tailored to their needs. Along the way, you'll see how advisors earn trust, develop lasting client relationships, and recommend insurance, investment, and wealth solutions that support a client's broader financial goals. Unlike many traditional internships, this program is built around real responsibility and practical application. You'll learn through experiencing and doing, not just observing. Our goal is to provide a depth of experience that helps you build valuable professional skills, understand what it takes to grow a business, and make a meaningful impact in the lives of others. By the end of the program, you'll have a clearer understanding of the advisor career path and the opportunity to determine whether it's the right fit for your future.Schedule: Flexible, designed to work around classes and other commitments Compensation: Up to $3,000 in activity-based pay, plus commission on sales. There is no salary or hourly compensation.ResponsibilitiesWhat You'll Learn Develop Career-Ready Skills Through Real Experience: Build communication, sales, relationship-building, and business development skills through hands-on training, coaching, mentorship, and real client interactions. Learn How to Help Clients Plan for What Matters: Gain exposure to Northwestern Mutual's planning approach and learn how insurance, investments, retirement planning, and other solutions can help clients achieve financial security. Explore an Entrepreneurial Career with Clarity: Get experience learning how business development, client relationships, accountability, and compensation contribute to long-term success. What You'll DoIn the Financial Services Sales Program, you'll: Develop foundational sales skills through hands-on client interactions, including hosting discovery conversations to understand their priorities and goals.Build a market of potential clients through prospecting, personal connections, referrals, and new relationships. Learn about Northwestern Mutual's holistic financial planning approach and how advisors develop recommendations across insurance, investments, retirement, and other financial decisions. Work alongside experienced financial advisors through mentorship and joint work opportunities. Secure required Life, Accident & Health insurance licensing By completing the available training in this program, including holding the College Agent’s Contract, meeting licensing requirements, building your network, conducting discovery conversations, participating in client planning activities, applying coaching feedback, and engaging in business development, you will be better positioned for success in this program or whatever career you may choose. How Compensation WorksCompensation is tied to completing sales- and business-focused program activities, including conducting financial discovery conversations and learning how advisors prepare personalized recommendations. Additional compensation takes the form of commissions from eligible sales. Here's how it works: You can earn up to $3,000 during the program based on completing sales and business development activities You also have the opportunity to earn commissions from sales There is no salary or hourly compensation QualificationsWho This Early-Career Program Is For We're looking for students who are: Currently enrolled full-time in college (juniors and seniors preferred) Interested in learning about financial planning, business development, entrepreneurship, or sales Comfortable building relationships and starting conversations with others Motivated by personal growth and professional development Able to independently manage priorities, responsibilities, and accountability Curious about exploring the financial representative career through direct experience rather than observation aloneEligible participants may be considered for a full-time financial representative role following graduation. Participants may also be considered for another role within their local network office

jobs.description: Employer: ATK Technologies Expires: 11/11/2026 AI Human Interactive Operation InternAbout Us: We are a future-minded AI hedging technology company developing responsible, sustainable software and hardware products designed to safeguard human connection as technology advances.We are launching CitaCoffee (www.CitaCoffee.com), a safety-first social meetup platform that helps people build authentic offline connections. In an increasingly digital yet socially isolated society, CitaCoffee’s mission is to combat loneliness and provide a secure, real-life meetup and dating tool that actively reduces online scams and catfishing.We are launching in southern California (LA County, Orange County, San Diego County) and recruiting motivated AI Human Interactive Operation Intern to bring our responsible dating and social meetup movement to college campuses and local communities. The Role: As an AI Human Interactive Operation Intern, you will drive organic user growth on your campus and in your local community through AI empowered offline interactive approaches, helping students transition conversations off their screens and into local coffee shops. Key Responsibilities:AI based outreach: analysis, and agent operation.User Acquisition: Pitch the CitaCoffee app to peers, clubs, and campus organizations.Event Activation: Plan and host engaging pop-up coffee events on or near campus that demonstrate the app's local matching feed, which keeps meetups within easy walking or driving distance.Local Partnerships: Collaborate with our growth team to secure local coffee-shop partnerships to serve as designated meetup spots, supporting word-of-mouth discovery.Product Feedback: Collect feedback from new users on the free tier and report key insights back to our product team. Who We're Looking For:Mindful, forward-thinking individuals passionate about human connection in the AI era.Currently enrolled student at an accredited 2-year or 4-year college/university in or near the Los Angeles or San Diego areas.Must be at least 18 years of age.Outgoing and confident approaching new people and talking with strangers about the product.Deeply familiar with local campus culture and coffee spots.Self-motivated starter capable of managing a flexible schedule and meeting weekly targets.Compensation & Schedule:Job Type: Internship (Part-Time / Flexible Hours)Pay Rate: $19.00 – $22.00 / hourLocation: Hybrid / On-Campus (Los Angeles & San Diego areas) How to Apply: Apply directly on Handshake, or complete your application on our official website at www.CitaCoffee.com by clicking the "Join Us" link. Veteran Welcome & Commitment: We strongly encourage student veterans, active military members, reservists, guard members, and military spouses to apply. We value the leadership, adaptability, teamwork, and strong ethic of service that veterans bring to our team and community initiatives.Equal Opportunity Employer Statement: We are an Equal Opportunity Employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees regardless of race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, veteran status, disability, age, or any other legally protected status.

We're WebFX, a full-service digital marketing agency based in the US. We've been 10x named the Best Place To Work in Pennsylvania, and we'd love to meet you! We are a fast-growing company that has doubled in size over the past 5 years, with talented team members now based around the globe (and representing 18+ different countries!). While we are growing at a rapid rate, we are committed to growing strategically and sustainably, and that starts with growing our team of the #BestCoworkers - that’s where you come in!We're looking for people to join our mission to provide world-class digital marketing solutions to mid-size businesses around the world. We are passionate about what we do, we’re committed to driving business growth for our clients, and we’re on the hunt for people just like you, who take pride in their work and want to be part of a company that does too.Why Choose WebFX?Vibrant Company Culture: We've been named the Best Place To Work in Pennsylvania 10 times Individual and Company Growth: Merit-based promotions with a clear progression path. WebFX grew 250% over the past 3 years, and we promote almost exclusively internallyTraining and Development: Entry-level roles, comprehensive training, ongoing learning programs, and the chance to learn from some of the best in the businessFlexible Schedule: Start your day between 8-10 am - when you do your best work Insurance Coverage: Health, vision, dental, and supplemental insurance with multiple plans and options to choose from, including HSA and FSA options with contribution matching 100% Company 401k Matching: Up to 4% Work-Life Balance: Generous PTO, new parent support (and paw-ternity leave!) Tech and Equipment: All technology & equipment provided - every FXer receives a tech set-up valued at ~$1500, plus a personal desk fund for any extra touches you want to add to your space! Health & Wellness: 24/7 on-site gym and an employee wellness program including a free FitBit, fitness challenges, and a Headspace account Office Perks: Complimentary coffee service by our on-site barista, tea bar, pet-friendly office spaces, casual dress code, surprise catered meals, and more Opportunities to Give Back: On top of charitable donation matching and local volunteer opportunities, our #FXBuilds program has positively impacted over 15,000 people around the world - and every individual FXer's work directly contributes...And So Much More! Home buyer program, profit sharing, personal desk fund, green commute benefits, and the opportunity to be part of a passionate, driven team where we pride ourselves on delivering high-quality work that makes a real-world impact for our clientsCheck out our culture on social media:InstagramTwitterFacebook*You don't need to apply more than once even if you're interested in multiple positions - you can simply let us know! We consider all open roles when reviewing resumes and applications!We have a multi-step interview process, where we focus on giving both our candidates, and ourselves, opportunities to get to know each other a bit better. While our process may be more thorough and perhaps longer than other interview processes that you've been a part of, our goal is to work together with our candidates to find a mutually beneficial fit, where a candidate is a great addition to the FXFamily, and WebFX is the right fit for their career goals. Interested in joining the FXFamily? You should definitely apply now!WebFX is an Equal Opportunity Employer, committed to providing and fostering an inclusive environment where all people, including women, minorities, LGBTQ+ and other underrepresented groups are supported, respected, and encouraged to excel within STEM careers. jobs.title: 2026/27 Analyst Program, Finance & Budgets (MBA) at New Jersey Turnpike Authority
jobs.description: Employer: New Jersey Turnpike Authority Expires: 11/12/2026 Job descriptionThe New Jersey Turnpike Authority has opportunities for students who will be enrolled in an undergraduate or graduate program. Analysts gain hands-on experience at our Woodbridge, NJ Headquarters.Positions in our Finance & Budgets department welcome majors that include but are not limited to Finance/Accounting, Computer Science, Business Administration, and related fields. Over the course of this internship, you will influence several of our Finance units. You will build skills translating data into opportunities, enhancing our risk and controls framework.Work may include applying data analytics to assess operational performance, developing business cases for new digital features, creating dashboards to track key metrics, and updating website content for core Authority services. Over the course of the 3 month internship, interns will be dedicated to one of the many functional groups within the Authority, allowing them to gain meaningful, hands-on experience within their assigned area. Depending on the group, exposure may include traffic and revenue analysis, toll collector audits, accounts receivable/payable processes, financial reporting, data analysis, and other operational and financial functions. ResponsibilitiesPartner with business leaders and enterprise service organizations to support product development and strategic decision-making.Build strong influencing and communication skills through collaboration with key stakeholders and leadership.Work with Technology teams to evaluate and improve processes, experiment with new ways of working, and leverage emerging technologies.Develop skills in financial modeling, data analytics, reporting automation, and data visualization tools.Provide analytical and operational support to assigned departments, including work on small projects or components of larger initiativesCollaborate with staff at various levels of the organization to complete tasks and assignments effectively.Apply data analytics to assess operational performance and support the development of business cases for new digital features.Create dashboards to track key metrics and assist with updates to content supporting core Authority services. Career ProgressionFull-Time/Part-Time Job Opportunities: Interns may transition to full-time, part-time, or Fall/Spring Aide positions. Do I have to be enrolled in school to apply?You must be a continuing/recent grad enrolled student to qualify. Masters and MBA only. What is the duration of the Finance Summer Aide program?year long. The NJTA works with students on flexible start/end dates based on a student’s leave and return dates to college (Fall and Spring opportunities will vary) Is this a remote or onsite position?The Analysts for the Finance & Budgets department will work onsite at the NJTA headquarters building located at 1 Turnpike Plaza, Woodbridge, NJ. Summer Analysts are not eligible to work remote. Is this a paid position?Yes. All Analysts will receive a rate based on years of education completed. The hourly rate is between $20/hr. and $23/hr. The standard work week is Monday to Friday.

jobs.title: Procurement Commodity Intern at Flowers Foods
jobs.description: Employer: Flowers Foods Expires: 11/12/2026 Procurement (Commodity) Intern Bringing Home the Dough$20 - $25 an hour—based on projected academic level at time of internship Location: Onsite/Hybrid —Thomasville, GA (Housing is not provided) Rising to the Challenge: Position ResponsibilitiesAs a Procurement Commodity Intern, you will support the Commodity team with market intelligence, consolidation opportunities, and planning and rollout of a complex RFP process. You will collect and analyze data, develop bid summaries, and make recommendations based on your findings. In this role, you will monitor and analyze key commodity markets, support development of market sensitivity models, and help identify trends and pricing opportunities. The Procurement Commodity Intern will build and maintain Excel-based analytical models, reports, and dashboards while supporting cross-functional teams, ad hoc analysis, and special projects. This role will allow personal and professional growth through meaningful projects that encourage the use of current and developing skills. jobs.title: 2027 Summer Internship Program - REIN Data Intern at Federal Reserve Bank of Atlanta
jobs.description: Employer: Federal Reserve Bank of Atlanta Expires: 11/12/2026 As an employee of the Atlanta Fed, you will help support our mission of promoting the stability and efficiency of the U.S. economy and financial system. Your work will affect the economy of the Southeast, the United States, and the world. The work we do here is important, and how we do it is just as important as what we do. We live our values of integrity, excellence, and respect every day. We do the right thing, we do things right, and we treat people right. A career at the Federal Reserve Bank of Atlanta gives you the chance to do work that touches lives and helps communities prosper. OUR BANK - The Federal Reserve is the central bank of the United States and is one of the most influential, trusted, and prestigious financial organizations. It consists of twelve Reserve Banks located around the country and the Board of Governors in Washington, D.C. The Federal Reserve Bank of Atlanta territory covers the Sixth Federal Reserve District, which includes Alabama, Florida, and Georgia, and portions of Louisiana, Mississippi, and Tennessee. The Atlanta Fed and the other Reserve Banks play an important part in all three of the Fed's functions: monetary policy, bank supervision and regulation, and the operation of a nationwide payment system. OUR PEOPLE - At the Federal Reserve Bank of Atlanta, we rely on the unique individual talents, expertise, and valued perspectives of our employees as well as those of external stakeholders to carry out our mission as part of the nation's central bank. PLEASE READ: Internships are paid. Housing will not be provided. This is not necessarily an exhaustive list of all responsibilities, duties, performance standards or requirements, efforts, skills or working conditions associated with the job. While this is intended to be an accurate reflection of the current job, management reserves the right to revise the job or to require that other or different tasks be performed when circumstances change (e.g. emergencies, rush jobs, change in workload or technological developments). SCOPE OF ASSIGNMENT: Under supervision, the selected intern may assist with some or all the following: Monitor, research, and manage data in the Customer Relationship Management (CRM) database Research prospective businesses Assist with administrative processes and required documentation updates Provide assistance with branch event coordination and support QUALIFICATIONS: Students must be currently enrolled at an accredited college or university in a Bachelor’s degree program through the duration of the internship. Minimum cumulative GPA above 2.75 in academically rigorous curriculum. Must be committed to working 15-20 hours a week for 10-12 weeks. With the possibility of extending to Spring semesterMinimum of 15hrs a week onsite PREFERRED MAJORS: Business Administration Economics Finance Math CORE COMPETENCIES: Proficient in Microsoft Office Suite Excellent communication skills (verbal and written) Strong technical skills Ability to work independently and take ownership of projects Great work ethic and detail oriented Comfortable working across time zones to complete projects in a timely manner TO APPLY: In addition to your application, please attach a resume and a copy of your most recent unofficial transcript. Additional Requirements: This position will require at minimum fingerprinting for a criminal background check, education and employment verification, along with potential additional screening requirements due to the information accessed while performing the job. Any offer of employment is contingent upon satisfactory results of any required background screening. These screenings would be initiated at the time of offer acceptance and can take up to approximately 8 weeks to be completed. The screening covers areas such as education/employment verification, criminal history, credit history, and reaches out to your references and people that know you well. For Law Enforcement positions, physical, psychological, drug, stress/EKG, and attending an academy will be required. Applicants must be currently authorized to work in the United States without the need for visa sponsorship now or in the future. Federal Reserve Bank of Atlanta employees must comply with the Bank’s ethics rules. These rules generally prohibit employees, their spouses/domestic partners, and minor children from holding financial interests (such as common stock and corporate bonds) issued by financial institutions. This prohibition also applies to investment funds that focus on investing in the financial sector. If you, your spouse/domestic partner, or minor child own such securities, you will generally be asked to divest them if you accept an offer of Bank employment. If you have concerns about this prohibition, you should raise the issue with the recruiter for this posting early in the process. This is not necessarily an exhaustive list of all responsibilities, duties, performance standards or requirements, efforts, skills or working conditions associated with the job. While this is intended to be an accurate reflection of the current job, management reserves the right to revise the job or to require that other or different tasks be performed when circumstances change (e.g. emergencies, rush jobs, change in workload or technological developments). The Federal Reserve Bank of Atlanta is an equal opportunity employer.

jobs.feedName: David Nazarian College of Business & Economics
jobs.title: Student Trainee Management and Program Analyst at U.S. Department of Energy
jobs.description: Employer: U.S. Department of Energy Expires: 11/12/2026 Student Trainee Management and Program AnalystLocation: Washington, District of Columbia, United States Work Model: Onsite Employment Type: Full-Time Position Type: InternshipThis internship is located in the Office of Energy Dominance Financing (EDF).Join DOE's Power Up program and kickstart your federal career! This program is designed to offer exciting early-career opportunities for upcoming professionals ready to make an impact in the Federal government.As a participant, you will be paired with an on-the-job mentor whose guidance is tailored specifically to your career path-whether you are entering a technical specialty or an administrative/professional role. In this program, mentoring goes far beyond basic job training. Your mentor will serve as a trusted guide, helping you build confidence, develop professional skills, and learn how to navigate and thrive within a structured, mission-driven environment.The U.S. Department of Energy's Office of Energy Dominance Financing (EDF) supports high-impact energy and manufacturing initiatives that advance U.S. energy security, affordability, grid reliability, and national competitiveness. EDF works closely with private-sector partners, other federal agencies, and key stakeholders to finance projects that strengthen America's energy foundation and support emerging technologies. As an EDF intern, you will gain unparalleled professional development by engaging in large-scale loan evaluations for innovative energy projects, building expertise in financial modeling, due diligence, and credit risk analysis. This opportunity provides a unique opportunity to contribute to the national good by directly supporting the revitalization and innovation of the U.S. energy industry, enabling the deployment of energy technologies and fostering American economic prosperity.EDF interns may participate in research, analysis, and program support across these focus areas, gaining exposure to federal energy finance, public-private partnerships, and cross-agency collaboration.As a Power Up Intern in the Office of Energy Dominance Financing (EDF), you will support our daily mission goals.EDF's work includes:- Energy generation and grid reliability projects- Innovative energy technology initiatives- Manufacturing and advanced transportation projects- Tribal energy investment and partnership projects- CO2 transportation and infrastructure projects- Energy solutions that support U.S. leadership in artificial intelligence and other emerging technologiesFor more information, visit Energy Dominance Financing Program | Department of Energy.

jobs.title: Wealth Management Intern at Integrated Private Wealth
jobs.description: Employer: Integrated Private Wealth Expires: 11/12/2026 Wealth Management Intern Advisor Support, Client Service and AI Workflows Location San Diego, CAPosition Paid, part-time internshipReports to Erick Conway, Financial AdvisorHourly rate [Approved range]Weekly hours [To be confirmed]Work arrangement and start date [To be confirmed] About the roleIntegrated Private Wealth is building a premier private wealth platform serving successful entrepreneurs, executives, and families with complex financial lives. The Wealth Management Intern will work closely with financial advisor Erick Conway to improve workflows, support client service, and learn how a wealth management practice operates. An early priority will be helping build and refine processes using AI agents and Quin, while shadowing Erick and learning the planning and investment strategies used with clients. This paid, part-time opportunity is designed for someone interested in a long-term financial planning career who brings practical AI experience, attention to detail, and a genuine commitment to service. The potential progression is from internship to full-time Client Service Associate and, over time, junior Financial Advisor. What success looks likeErick spends less time coordinating routine administration. Client information and follow-ups are accurate and organized, and approved AI workflows reduce repetitive work without compromising quality. The intern demonstrates growing knowledge, sound judgment, and readiness for broader responsibility. Key responsibilitiesAI workflows and process improvementWork with Erick to map recurring tasks and identify opportunities to improve meeting preparation, follow-up, documentation, and client onboarding.Help configure, test, and refine AI agents and Quin-supported workflows; document instructions, review outputs for accuracy, and recommend practical improvements.Use firm-approved tools and authorized information only. Obtain approval before implementing automations or using them for client communications or account activity. Advisor and meeting supportCoordinate scheduling, meeting logistics, agendas, and background materials for selected client, prospect, and professional-partner meetings.Shadow Erick in selected meetings, capture action items, and prepare follow-up drafts for review.Track commitments, maintain organized records, and alert Erick to unresolved items, changing priorities, or potential delays. Client onboarding and service supportAssist with document collection, account-opening paperwork, asset-transfer follow-up, and routine client requests under supervision.Maintain accurate client information, notes, tasks, and service status in approved systems; coordinate handoffs with IPW client-service colleagues.Learn the end-to-end onboarding and service process for relationships Erick leads. Client advice, recommendations, and transaction authorizations remain with authorized professionals. Learning and professional developmentLearn how planning, investments, tax considerations, estate planning, and client service fit together through shadowing, assigned research, and coaching.Apply feedback, document what you learn, and build the knowledge and judgment needed for increasing responsibility. Qualifications RequiredRelevant coursework in financial planning, finance, business, economics, accounting, or a related field, with a clear interest in a financial planning career.Hands-on experience creating, configuring, and using AI agents or automated workflows. Coursework, personal projects, internships, and professional experience may demonstrate this capability.Strong organization, attention to detail, written and verbal communication, and comfort learning new technology.Dependability, punctuality, discretion, and a willingness to learn, follow instructions, investigate routine problems, and ask for guidance when needed. PreferredCollege senior expecting to graduate in May 2027, with interest in potential full-time employment in San Diego by summer 2027.Experience in client service, administrative support, financial services, or another professional environment.Familiarity with Quin, CRM systems, workflow tools, or financial-planning software; experience documenting processes and testing AI outputs. Prior wealth management employment or an advanced technical background is not required. Candidates should be prepared to discuss an AI agent or workflow they have built, what it accomplished, and how they checked its accuracy. Key competencies Client Mindset Approaches every interaction with care, responsiveness, and professionalism; understands that reliable follow-through is part of excellent service. Stewardship Takes ownership of assigned work, communicates status, and follows commitments through to completion within the scope of training and supervision. jobs.description: Employer: KWH Constructors, Inc. Expires: 11/12/2026 Estimating Intern | Bridge & Heavy Civil Construction — Estimating Learn how bridges get priced, bid, and won—from the people who build them.Reports To: Project Manager Location: Issaquah, WA, with potential site visits to West Coast and Alaska projects Eligibility: Rising Juniors and Seniors currently enrolled in an accredited Civil Engineering, Construction Management, or related programWhy You’ll Love This Role ✓ Genuinely hands-on — you’ll work on real bids, not just shadow or file paperwork. ✓ 1:1 mentorship from experienced bridge and heavy civil estimators. ✓ Pre-bid site walks and visits to active projects, where you see how the work you helped price actually gets built. ✓ Exposure to a wide range of bridge work — new structures, replacements, widenings, seismic retrofits, and rehabilitation. ✓ Strong potential path to a full-time Junior Estimator offer, after graduation. ✓ Competitive pay: $25.00 – $30.00 per hour, plus [housing/travel stipend if applicable].Who Thrives HereAs an Estimating Intern, you’ll get a real, hands-on introduction to bridge and heavy civil estimating — working alongside senior estimators, project managers, and engineers to turn plans and specifications into competitive, buildable bids. You’re detail-oriented, comfortable with numbers, and curious about how things get built and what they cost. This internship is built to give you a strong technical foundation through real bid work, mentorship, candid feedback, and purposeful learning.What You’ll Do • Quantity Takeoffs: Help perform takeoffs from plans and specifications for bridge elements such as structural concrete, reinforcing steel, girders, piling, drilled shafts, excavation, and falsework, with review from a senior estimator. • Pricing & Quotes: Help request and track subcontractor and supplier quotes, and assist in building bid-day quote comparison sheets. • Bid Support: Track addenda, bid questions, and deadlines, and assist with bid forms and documentation for state DOT and local agency bids. • Project Site Experience: Join pre-bid meetings, site walks, and active project visits to see how site conditions, access, and means and methods drive cost and schedule. • Team Collaboration: Sit in on bid reviews and team meetings, and learn how estimators, project managers, and our temporary works engineers work together to build an estimate. • Ownership & Contribution: Take responsibility for your assigned tasks, ask questions when you need context, and contribute your ideas to the team. What Your Internship Looks Like • Weeks 1–2: Onboarding — learn our estimating tools, cost database, bid process, and how the estimating team operates through a bid cycle. • Ongoing: Work alongside a senior estimator on live bids — takeoffs, quote tracking, and bid-day support. Real bid work, not busywork. • By the end: Walk away with real estimating experience, a mentor network, and — for strong performers — a conversation about a full-time Junior Estimator role after graduation.Minimum Requirements • Currently pursuing a Bachelor’s degree in Civil Engineering, Construction Management, or a related field, with Junior standing (or equivalent credit hours) and 1–2 years remaining before graduation.Desired Qualifications • Completed coursework in statics, construction methods, or cost estimating. Coursework in structural design or project controls preferred. • Proficiency in Microsoft Office, especially Excel. Familiarity with Bluebeam, AutoCAD, or estimating software such as HCSS HeavyBid or B2W Estimate preferred. • Prior construction experience (field, internship, or summer work) preferred. • Involvement in student organizations such as ASCE or an AGC student chapter, or construction/estimating competition teams, preferred.
